title: [Audit] 🔐 Identity & Access
description: Who authenticated, how, from where, and what failed. Resolves the numeric user.name into real identities.

config.description: Distinct identities in all traffic, resolved as email, then API key name, then user.name — one per row of Identity first and last seen. The line under the number splits them: humans have an email on their events (the Humans tile), machines do not (service accounts, API keys, internal and anonymous principals).

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | STATS `Identities` = COUNT_DISTINCT(actor), human = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.user.email), machine = COUNT_DISTINCT(actor) WHERE attributes.user.email IS NULL | EVAL detail = CONCAT(CASE(human == 0, "no humans", human == 1, "1 human", CONCAT(TO_STRING(human), " humans")), " · ", CASE(machine == 0, "no machine", machine == 1, "1 machine", CONCAT(TO_STRING(machine), " machine"))) | KEEP `Identities`, detail

config.description: Distinct email addresses in all traffic — the people Busiest human identities ranks. An Elasticsearch API key carries its creator's email, so a person can count here through a key they made without signing in; the line under the number says how many signed in through SAML SSO.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS `Humans` = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.user.email), sso = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.user.email) WHERE attributes.user.domain == "cloud-saml-kibana" | EVAL detail = CASE(sso == 0, "none signed in by SSO", CONCAT(TO_STRING(sso), " signed in by SSO")) | KEEP `Humans`, detail

config.description: Distinct API keys seen in range, of both kinds: Elastic Cloud API keys (recorded by id only) and Elasticsearch (ES) API keys (by id and name); the line under the number splits them. One per row of API key inventory. A re-issued Elasticsearch key keeps its name under a new id and counts again.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.api_key.id IS NOT NULL OR attributes.user.domain == "_cloud_api_key" | STATS es = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.api_key.id), cloud = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.user.name) WHERE attributes.api_key.id IS NULL | EVAL `API keys` = es + cloud, detail = CASE(es + cloud == 0, "none in range", CONCAT(CASE(cloud == 0, "no Cloud", cloud == 1, "1 Cloud", CONCAT(TO_STRING(cloud), " Cloud")), " · ", CASE(es == 0, "no ES", es == 1, "1 ES", CONCAT(TO_STRING(es), " ES")))) | KEEP `API keys`, detail

config.description: Events authenticated through the cloud-saml-kibana SAML realm — a person in a browser. The line under the number counts Kibana user_login events: a session that began before the range shows events here but no new sign-in.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.user.domain == "cloud-saml-kibana" | STATS `SSO events` = COUNT(*), logins = COUNT(*) WHERE attributes.event.action == "user_login" | EVAL detail = CASE(logins == 0, "no new sign-ins", logins == 1, "1 new sign-in", CONCAT(TO_STRING(logins), " new sign-ins")) | KEEP `SSO events`, detail

config.description: Failed sign-ins (authentication_failed, realm_authentication_failed, anonymous_access_denied) plus requests refused or failed after sign-in (access_denied and any failed outcome). The line under the number splits the two — failed logins, then denied (refused or failed after sign-in): a denial is an authenticated identity hitting a permission wall, not someone guessing credentials. Same predicate as the two failure panels below.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_failed","realm_authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied") OR attributes.event.outcome == "failure" | STATS `Failed or denied` = COUNT(*), signin = COUNT(*) WHERE attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_failed","realm_authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied") | EVAL after = `Failed or denied` - signin, detail = CONCAT(CASE(signin == 0, "no logins", signin == 1, "1 login", CONCAT(TO_STRING(signin), " logins")), " · ", CASE(after == 0, "none denied", CONCAT(TO_STRING(after), " denied"))) | KEEP `Failed or denied`, detail

config.description: Distinct Kibana browser sessions observed in range, and how many people (by email) they belong to.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.kibana.session.id IS NOT NULL | STATS `Kibana sessions` = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.kibana.session.id), people = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.user.email) | EVAL detail = CASE(`Kibana sessions` == 0, "none in range", CASE(people == 0, "no email recorded", people == 1, "1 person", CONCAT(TO_STRING(people), " people"))) | KEEP `Kibana sessions`, detail

config.title: Authentication method over time
config.description: Elasticsearch requests per interval by how they presented credentials: API key, token (SSO browser sessions and service accounts) or realm (username and password). One bar per credential type per interval, on a log scale, so a type carrying a fraction of a percent of the traffic is as readable as the bulk; an interval with no bar had no requests of that type. A shift in this mix is worth explaining.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.authentication.type IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY BUCKET(@timestamp, 75, ?_tstart, ?_tend), attributes.authentication.type | EVAL auth = CASE(attributes.authentication.type == "api_key", "API key", attributes.authentication.type == "token", "Token", attributes.authentication.type == "realm", "Realm", attributes.authentication.type == "saml", "SAML", attributes.authentication.type == "anonymous", "Anonymous", attributes.authentication.type == "internal", "Internal", attributes.authentication.type) | SORT auth

config.title: Credential type by identity
config.description: Which credential type each of the 12 busiest identities presents; the stronger the fill, the more events (log scale; the legend lists the decades the chart spans). Humans should authenticate by token (SSO); service identities by API key. Only Elasticsearch requests record a credential type, so identities seen only in Kibana or only anonymously are counted in Identities above but are not on this chart. A Cloud API key has no name and is shown by its id.

config.title: Events by identity origin
config.description: Share of events, not of identities, by the email on the event: Elastic (@elastic.co), Tenant (any other address), or Machine (no email: service accounts, Cloud API keys, internal users and anonymous requests). One busy key can make Machine nearly all of it while most identities are people. An Elasticsearch API key carries its creator's email, so traffic from a key a person created counts under that person's origin.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY attributes.user.email | EVAL actor_org = CASE(attributes.user.email IS NULL, "Machine", attributes.user.email LIKE "*@elastic.co", "Elastic", "Tenant") | STATS events = SUM(events) BY origin = actor_org

config.title: Events by authentication realm
config.description: Share of events by the security realm that authenticated them. SAML SSO is interactive human sign-in (cloud-saml-kibana); Elasticsearch API key (_es_api_key) and Cloud API key (_cloud_api_key) are programmatic — an Elasticsearch key minted by a Cloud API key authenticates in the Cloud key's realm; Service account is Elastic's own components (_service_account). Any other realm is shown by its name.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.user.domain IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY attributes.user.domain | EVAL realm = CASE(attributes.user.domain == "cloud-saml-kibana", "SAML SSO", attributes.user.domain == "_es_api_key", "Elasticsearch API key", attributes.user.domain == "_cloud_api_key", "Cloud API key", STARTS_WITH(attributes.user.domain, "_service_account"), "Service account", STARTS_WITH(attributes.user.domain, "_"), "Other internal", attributes.user.domain) | STATS events = SUM(events) BY realm

config.title: Busiest API keys
config.description: The busiest API keys of both kinds, one row per key, with request volume and how many distinct client IPs used it. Kind is Cloud (an Elastic Cloud API key: no name, recorded by its id) or Elasticsearch (an Elasticsearch API key: id and name). A key used from many IPs is worth investigating. A re-issued key keeps its name under a new id, so a name can appear twice. The full list, with owner and first and last use, is API key inventory below.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.api_key.id IS NOT NULL OR attributes.user.domain == "_cloud_api_key" | STATS events = COUNT(*), ips = COUNT_DISTINCT(client.ip) BY attributes.api_key.name, attributes.api_key.id, attributes.user.name | EVAL key_id = COALESCE(attributes.api_key.id, attributes.user.name), api_key = COALESCE(attributes.api_key.name, "(no name)"), kind = CASE(attributes.api_key.id IS NULL, "Cloud", "Elasticsearch") | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 9

config.title: Busiest human identities
config.description: People by email, busiest first: the people the Humans tile counts, over all traffic, with the same event counts as Identity first and last seen, which also has when each was first and last seen. The panel shows the top rows; the rest are in that session. Click an email to pin that person across the suite.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*), ips = COUNT_DISTINCT(client.ip) BY attributes.user.email | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: Most frequent failed or denied access · none is good
config.description: Failed sign-ins and refused requests grouped by identity, action and source IP, most frequent first; the top rows of what the Failed or denied tile counts. authentication_failed, realm_authentication_failed and anonymous_access_denied are failed sign-ins; access_denied is an authenticated identity refused an action; any other action is marked "· failed" — it is here because its outcome was failure. An Identity that reads as an opaque id is a principal whose events carry no email and no key name — usually an organisation-level Elastic Cloud API key, which the audit stream records only by its id. An empty panel means nothing matched in the time range, which is the healthy state.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_failed","realm_authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied") OR attributes.event.outcome == "failure" | STATS events = COUNT(*), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, action = attributes.event.action, ip = client.ip | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | STATS events = SUM(events), last_seen = MAX(last_seen) BY actor, action, ip | EVAL action = CASE(action IN ("authentication_failed","realm_authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied", "access_denied"), action, CONCAT(COALESCE(action, "(no action)"), " · failed")) | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: Failed sign-ins and denied access, newest 1,000 · none is good
config.description: The newest failed sign-ins and refused requests, record by record. Discover stops at 1,000 rows, so on a busy range its result count is that cap and the Failed or denied tile is the total. Result names the kind: failed sign-in, denied (access_denied), or failed (any other failed outcome). An Identity that reads as an opaque id is a principal whose events carry no email and no key name — usually an organisation-level Elastic Cloud API key, which the audit stream records only by its id. An empty panel means nothing matched in the time range, which is the healthy state.

config.title: API key inventory
config.description: Every API key seen in range (up to 1,000), Cloud and Elasticsearch, busiest first — one row per key the API keys tile counts — with owner, volume, IP spread, indices touched and first and last use. Owner is the identity that created the key: a person's email, or for a key minted programmatically the id of the Cloud API key that minted it (its own row reads "(no name)"); a Cloud API key's own creator is not in the audit stream, so its Owner reads Cloud organisation.

config.title: Identity first and last seen
config.description: Every identity in range (up to 1,000), all traffic — one row per identity the Identities tile counts — with its first and last appearance, Events (everything it did, the same count as Busiest human identities) and Signal events (what is left after the noise gate, the count the gated panels across the suite use). Newest first appearance on top. Widen the time range to tell a brand-new identity from one that was simply quiet. An Identity that reads as an opaque id is a principal whose events carry no email and no key name — usually an organisation-level Elastic Cloud API key, which the audit stream records only by its id.
